rubric.result: The objective promises four things and each has production lines behind it. (a) 'parses the body the form sends': `CoordinatingSessionRoute.opening` calls `PlanRequest.from(JsonBody.textOf(request))` and, when the outcome is not ACCEPTED, answers `PlanRefusal.of(asked)` — so `id`, `user_comment`, `repo` and `path` keep the codes the plan asked them to keep (the `nothing-to-plan` test proves it end to end). (b) 'refuses a repository list': `if (asked.listed) { Answer.refuseAs(response, CoordinatingSessionRefusal.of(CoordinatingSessionOutcome.ONE_REPOSITORY_ONLY)) }`, 400 with detail 'an epic governs one checkout: send repo and path instead of repo_list'. (c) 'opens the conversation and holds it': `open.execute(new OpenCoordinatingSessionParams({story, comment, repository, root}))` inside a try that collapses a `PlanFailure` through `PlanCollapse.of`, then `held.remember(new HeldCoordinatingSession({state: CoordinatingSessionState.LIVE, conversation, session, attention: SessionAttention.working()}))` and a 202 carrying status/conversation/repo/root/session. (d) 'the entrypoint wires every adapter': `ct-api.ts` builds `ClaudeConversations` (liveSessions, shell, env, `~/.claude`, readdirSync/readFileSync, randomUUID, hooksUrl), `LocalSettingsSessionHooks`, `DiskConversationRecords` under `asked.stateRoot`, `CoordinatingSessions` and a real `OpenCoordinatingSession`, and hands the last two to `ApiServer`, which registers the route. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The **TDD:** line names two tests and fixes their assertions. `it('answers 202 with the conversation and the session it opened')` is in the diff: a real listening server (`new ApiServer({port: 0, ...})` + `server.start()` + `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:<port>/coordinating-session')`), the use case doubled by construction (`OpenCoordinatingSessionSpy extends OpenCoordinatingSession`), and the assertion on the literal body — `expect(response.status).toBe(202)` and `toEqual({status: 'brainstorming', conversation: Mother.CONVERSATION.id.text, repo: Mother.REPOSITORY.text, root: Mother.ROOT.text, session: {id: Mother.SESSION.id, name: Mother.SESSION.name}})`, over the literal request body `{"user_comment":…,"repo":"josemerca/ct-loop-sandbox","path":"/repo"}`. The second, `it('refuses a repository list because an epic governs one checkout')`, sends a `repo_list` body and asserts 400 with `{code: 'one-repository-only', detail: …}` and, as the sentence demands, that the use case was never asked: `expect(open.asked).toEqual([])`. Same assertion, same input, same expected value as the plan wrote down.

Walked name by name against both Contract blocks. coordinating-sessions.ts: `HeldCoordinatingSession` with `state`, `conversation: CoordinatingConversation`, `session: LiveSession | null`, `attention: SessionAttention | null` ✔ (frozen at construction); `CoordinatingSessions` with `constructor({stderr}: {stderr: (line: string) => void})` ✔, `remember(held): void` ✔, `held(): HeldCoordinatingSession | null` ✔, `attend({conversation: string, attention: SessionAttention}): boolean` ✔ — it returns false when nothing is held or `current.conversation.id.text !== conversation`, and on an accepted transition rebuilds the held session and writes exactly `coordinating session ${conversation} ${attention.status}\n` to the injected stderr, which is the brief's `coordinating session <id> <status>`. `CoordinatingSessionState` is the frozen pair `{LIVE: 'live', UNRESUMABLE: 'unresumable'}` beside `HeldCoordinatingSession` ✔. coordinating-session-route.ts: `CoordinatingSessionOutcome` frozen with `ACCEPTED: 'accepted'` and `ONE_REPOSITORY_ONLY: 'one-repository-only'` ✔; `CoordinatingSessionRoute.PATH = '/coordinating-session'` ✔, `METHODS = 'GET, POST'` ✔, `static opening(open: OpenCoordinatingSession, held: CoordinatingSessions): RequestHandler` ✔. The prose of the task is honoured too: `PlanRequest.from` parses, `PlanRefusal` carries the four field codes, `PlanCollapse` collapses the `PlanFailure` (the test proves `ConversationNotStarted` reaches `conversation-not-started` with the exception's own message), success is 202 with status `brainstorming` and the session held `live` and working, and `refusal-codes.test.ts` adds `CoordinatingSessionOutcome` to `RequestVocabularies.codes()`. One deliberate narrowing: the block writes `readonly state: string` and the diff writes `readonly state: CoordinatingSessionStateValue` — the vocabulary type the same block asks for, which is what `conventions/defects.md` requires of a value that classifies; the yardstick has precedence and no other name changed.

Row by row over the rows this diff bears on. D-26 ('the idea enters as a Jira user story or as free text … an epic governs one checkout'): the entrance accepts `id` and/or `user_comment` through `PlanRequest`, refuses `repo_list` with `one-repository-only`, and the story is relayed to the use case as `asked.story` for the `UserStories` adapter — implemented with that value. D-25 ('paths, never text pasted into a prompt'): the route passes story/comment/repository/root to the use case and never composes prompt text; `ct-api.ts` wires `DiskConversationRecords` whose `prepare` returns a path. D-10: both new modules are `.ts`, erasable syntax only, and `npm --prefix backend run typecheck` is green. D-21 is served in part (the held session is the thing `GET` will read in task 9) and contradicted nowhere. D-22: no gate endpoint is added. D-1, D-18 and the entrance button's literal are rows this diff leaves alone, which complies. No row is implemented with a different value.

EXEMPLARS: `start-plan-route.ts` — same shape of controller (`PlanRequest.from(JsonBody.textOf(request))`, early `Answer.refuseAs`, `try/catch` that rethrows anything that is not a `PlanFailure`, `Answer.send(response, 202, …)`); `session-input-route.ts` — the `Projection`-backed refusal class exported beside its route, matched by `CoordinatingSessionRefusal`, and `refuseOtherMethods` setting `Allow` before a 405 `{code, detail}`; `plan-events-route.ts` — an in-memory registry beside its route, matched by `coordinating-sessions.ts`; `sessions-route.test.ts` — the new test file mirrors it line for line (a `RunningApi` with `#started`, `NO_FRONTEND`, `stopAll` in `afterEach`, a spy subclassing the use case whose `super` receives bare port instances). RULES: `conventions/style.md` — no comment or docstring anywhere in the diff, every identifier and every diagnostic in English, and every function hangs off a type (statics on `CoordinatingSessionRoute`, `CoordinatingSessionRefusal`, `Mother`, `RunningApi`; methods on `CoordinatingSessions`); `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` refuses the declared-debt exemption here and the new modules need none. `conventions/architecture.md` — infrastructure controller named `<endpoint>-route.ts`, one file per endpoint, with its outcome vocabulary and its refusal projection inside it; `coordinating-sessions.ts` is the registry two endpoints will share, so it is a module of its own rather than living inside one endpoint's file; the use case is untouched and the route depends on it by construction. `conventions/boundaries.md` — 'the outer edge of the program … is the only place that assembles the dependency graph': `ct-api.ts` picks the concrete adapters and injects them, and the projection outward is exhaustive and returns a value object (`Projection('refusal', …)` raising for a member nobody mapped), with the code declared explicitly beside its detail and never derived from a class name. `backend/conventions/this-repository.md`'s HTTP rules — an application refusal answers 400, a protocol refusal keeps its own status (405 with `Allow`), every body is `{code, detail}`, every code kebab-case, and `refusal-codes.test.ts` now proves `one-repository-only` collides with nothing. `conventions/decisions.md` — the entrance's well-formedness is decided in one place (`PlanRequest`) rather than re-derived here. DEFECTS.MD, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — `CoordinatingSessionOutcome` and `CoordinatingSessionState` are frozen vocabularies, `HeldCoordinatingSession.state` is typed by the vocabulary rather than `string`, the dispatch is a `Projection` that raises instead of a catch-all, and no classifying value is compared by hand; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — the only maps are the 202 payload and the `{code, detail}` refusal handed to `Answer.send`, one step before the wire; `CoordinatingSessions` returns `HeldCoordinatingSession`, a type, and the use case returns `CoordinatingSessionOpened`; (3) two fields that have to agree — no sentinel: absence is `null` in the type (`held()` answers `null`, `session`/`attention` are nullable in the type) and no flag repeats what another field says. The one representable-but-incoherent pair, `state: LIVE` beside `session: null`, is written verbatim in the task's Contract block, so the diff could not have carried the absence in the state itself without failing item 3 — declared here, not a finding; (4) an error named for where it happens — the diff declares no error and reuses `ConversationNotStarted`, named for what happens. TWO CLASHES BETWEEN THE PLAN AND THESE DOCUMENTS, DECLARED AND LEFT OUT OF THE FINDINGS because no other diff was available to the implementer: (i) `conventions/architecture.md` says 'what every endpoint would otherwise repeat lives in a module of its own, never inside an endpoint's own file', and the parsing this route now shares (`PlanRequest`, `PlanRefusal`, `PlanCollapse`) still lives inside `start-plan-route.ts`; the task's own text orders that reuse and `start-plan-route.ts` is not in `**Files:**`, so extracting it was closed to this task; (ii) `conventions/simplicity.md` ('a public symbol … answers to a call that exists') is not discharged by `METHODS = 'GET, POST'` while GET is refused 405 today, by `CoordinatingSessionOutcome.ACCEPTED`, which nothing reads, or by `attend`, whose first caller is task 8's `/session-hooks` — all three are literal lines of the Contract block, and the implementer declared the last one in the task report. Beyond the three I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` and its `testing-anti-patterns.md`: none of its five anti-patterns fits — no assertion on mock existence, no test-only method added to a production class, the only double is the use case the layer is supposed to double, the doubled result is a complete `CoordinatingSessionOpened` built from real value objects, and the spy is eleven lines against six tests.
